cells.tense: You are here in the clearing, and each thing still standing is legible to you.
cells.act: put the frame on the table before anyone asks
cells.ask: Name the ending out loud — what's finished and what stays. One sentence, said once, no argument after it. Declare it plainly to whoever shares that space, before the question reaches you.
cells.core:
An ending is underway, and you can see the whole shape of it — what's finished, what isn't, and which is which. That's what makes the clearing go well. When it's working, you say the shape out loud once, and the bracing stops. Nobody has to guess where the edge of the ending sits.

What this balance can feed next is the frame, said in the open. Take one ending you're already inside and put it into a single sentence you say where it can be heard — this is over, this stays. Say it once. It doesn't have to be gentle. It has to be yours, spoken without waiting for permission or permission's cousin, explanation.
cells.sheetLine: Say the edge of the ending out loud, once.
cells.verb: holding many true things at once, seeing each one clearly
cells.place: where what must end is being cleared before what comes next can start

cells.tense: You'll be rehearsing every way the ending could still go wrong before it has had a chance to happen.
cells.act: face one way for three days
cells.ask: Choose the ending that's genuinely underway and hold your direction toward it for three days. Face that way only. Stop comparing it against the other versions you've been carrying.
cells.core:
There's a clearing underway, and every possible version of how it goes is being mapped ahead of time. Each one has its own true detail, so none of them gets set down. The clearing hasn't started; you're still measuring the field while the moment for walking through it comes and goes.

Pick a heading from what you actually want, not from the tally of risks, and face that one way for three days. Stop checking the other versions. Something at the end of those three days will have settled or it won't, and either way you'll be standing where you actually are, not inside the version you've been bracing against.

cells.tense: You were at a threshold that has already closed, and you're still standing in the frame of it.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Hand the task to two sets of hands — find one person and do the next piece of the ending together, side by side, until it moves. Don't run the work alone.
cells.core:
The ending is happening, and part of you has stepped back from it. You can still read what's ending clearly, and the reading is accurate. But nothing gets carried forward out of it, and the tank the clearing runs on is nearly empty.

Charging the tank directly doesn't work; pushing harder just empties it faster. What does work is joining someone in the small work of it. Find one person and do the next piece together — no briefing, no performance, both of you on the same part at the same time. The load lightens when two people carry the same thing, and the step after that tends to surface underneath it.

cells.tense: You've been making the fair calls about what to let go of throughout, while your own version has you only watching from the side.
cells.act: let the inner compass decide the small case
cells.ask: Listen for what feels owed inside this ending — not reasoned out, just felt — and act on the smallest piece of it. No announcement, no second opinion, no paperwork.
cells.core:
Endings near you come out clean, and when you describe how, the story has the situation settling itself. But something in you keeps knowing what's owed, what's finished, what it would be fair to release — and that knowing has been steering the clearing without your name on the record.

Try trusting the quiet call in one small case. There's an imbalance inside this ending you've been keeping level without noticing you were. Rather than reasoning it out, listen for what actually feels right about it, and act on that. Not the large case, the small one. Settle it this week without setting the record straight afterward. Whatever you choose, the clearing keeps working.
